name: From Shutdown Resistance to Self-Continuation Control: Identifiability, Intervention Stability, and Evidence Standards for Artificial Agents
headline: From Shutdown Resistance to Self-Continuation Control
publicationStatus: draft; not submitted; not peer reviewed; no DOI assigned
description: A continuation-specific identification framework for distinguishing observable shutdown resistance from stronger claims about stable current-bearer continuation control. The work combines exact counterexamples, synthetic learned-policy stress tests, intervention stability analysis, a domain-relative mechanism certificate, and a retrospective ROGUE benchmark audit.
primaryContribution: A layered evidence standard linking bearer identification, consequence representation, predictive retention, installed policy use, task-path blocking, reward-relevant joint consequences, held-out intervention stability, and domain/hypothesis-class mechanism certification.
explicitNonClaims: The manuscript does not establish that current frontier models intrinsically value their own continued existence.
The manuscript does not establish that shutdown resistance is always self-preservation.
The manuscript does not establish consciousness, negative valence, or fear of death in current AI systems.
The synthetic Q variable is an evaluator-declared bearer-role variable, not proof of an actual model self.
evidenceClasses: conditional UCT interpretation kept separate from functional results
futureArchivePolicy: If later archived with a DOI, preserve this v0.3 manuscript identity and provenance; do not silently replace it with a revised text.
